bullets.title: NVDA $500B AI Financing Partnership—Circular or Strategic?
bullets.body: Nvidia reportedly partnering with Apollo, Blackstone, BlackRock (GIP), Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR to mobilize over $500B in AI infrastructure financing, framed as bringing institutional capital into the buildout. Skeptics like Michael Burry and Ed Zitron labeled it a 'circle jerk SPV' hiding weak free cash flow, while Jensen Huang directly addressed the circular-financing concern in a CNBC appearance. Analyst confirms commitment sizes in the billions; no binding contracts yet, per Doug Kass (only an MOU).

bullets.title: Intel Upsizes $20B Share Sale on Record AI Demand; Capex Raised
bullets.body: Intel priced an upsized $20B equity offering at ~$95/share (6.5% discount) on demand exceeding $100B; CEO invested ~$12M personally. The raise funds foundry and AI infrastructure expansion, with capex guidance raised to $20B. Patrick Moorhead notes orders already fully subscribed; UBS models an Intel-AMD foundry partnership.

bullets.title: Berkshire Re-Enters Equity Buying, Adds 48.1M GOOGL Shares
bullets.body: Berkshire Hathaway ended 14 consecutive quarters as a net seller by buying $23.47B of equities vs. $3.69B sold in Q2 2026. Biggest buy: 48.1M Alphabet Class A shares, making GOOGL its third-largest position at ~$37B. Multiple hedge funds (Druckenmiller, Baupost, TCI) also added GOOGL in Q2; Li Lu now has ~50% of his portfolio in GOOGL. Berkshire also initiated D.R. Horton, exited Constellation Brands.

bullets.title: Gavin Baker's Q2 Portfolio: $821M MU, $1.9B NVDA, SpaceX Dominant
bullets.body: Gavin Baker's Altimeter Capital holds NVDA as its largest position (~19% at $1.9B), followed by TSM ($700M). New buys include MU and GOOGL; exits include AVGO, META, UBER, ARM. Separately, his public portfolio includes 711K shares of Micron ($821M) and 402K shares of Meta ($227M), plus a $4.67B SpaceX stake.

bullets.title: NBIS Blowout Q2: 454% YoY Revenue, $3.0-3.4B 2026 Guidance
bullets.body: Nebius Group Q2 revenue hit $582.3M (+454% YoY, +46% QoQ), beating $557M consensus; adjusted EBITDA $236M (vs. $158M est) with ~50% margin in AI Cloud. Full-year guidance set at $3.0–3.4B with EoY ARR of $7–9B. Situational Awareness (Leopold) fund—which was heavily long NBIS—suffered a 67% loss in Q2 and faced margin calls per 13F filings. Multiple hedge funds (Lone Pine at 7.2%, D1 initiating) are now top holders.

bullets.title: COHR Q4 FY26: First $2B Quarter; CPO Scale-Up H2 2027
bullets.body: Coherent Q4 FY26 revenue reached $2.05B (+34% YoY, +13% QoQ), at the top of guidance. Non-GAAP gross margin 40.2%, EPS $1.74 (+74% YoY). Q1 FY27 guidance: $2.2B–$2.4B midpoint. Key call highlight: InP substrate is now the primary supply constraint—above transceiver assembly—and management flagged they'll need more merchant InP substrate. CPO scale-up ramp reiterated for H2 2027. Jefferies raises PT to $420.

bullets.title: LITE Achieves First $1B Quarter; UHP Laser Demand Surging
bullets.body: Lumentum Q4 FY26: revenue $1.006B (+24.5% QoQ, +109% YoY), non-GAAP EPS $3.23 (vs. $2.97 est), gross margin 50.4%, operating margin 36.6%. Q1 FY27 guidance: $1.225B–$1.275B. CEO stated company is 'way behind shipments on high-powered lasers' and demand signal has increased. New products include NPO dialogue and OCS. CIEN and NOK highlighted as key beneficiaries.

bullets.title: SMCI Q4 FY26: $65-72B FY27 Guidance; $60B+ New Orders
bullets.body: Super Micro Computer Q4 FY26 EPS $1.70 (vs. $1.59 est), revenue $11.12B below $11.26B guide. Raised Q1 FY27 revenue guidance to $14.5B–$15.5B vs. $11.99B consensus. FY27 guidance: $65–72B vs. $52.4B consensus. CEO said nine customers with $1B+ revenues (up from four in FY25) and $60B+ new orders. JP Morgan raised PT to $45.

bullets.title: CRWV Q2: Revenue Doubles to $2.58B; Backlog Hits $104B
bullets.body: CoreWeave Q2 revenue reached $2.58B (vs. $2.56B est), more than doubling YoY. Loss per share $1.14 (vs. $1.41 est). Backlog surged to $104B including $25B+ in early Q3 customer commitments. Cloud revenue $126M beat estimate. Q3 guidance $214–216M. Stock surged 12–20% AH. Lone Pine made NBIS its new top position while D1 Capital initiated.

bullets.title: TSMC July Revenue +45% YoY; CoWoS Yields Clear 99%
bullets.body: TSMC July revenue hit $14.5B (+45% YoY), reaching a record; first-7-months revenue $89.1B (+37% YoY). CoWoS capacity doubled annually for 3 consecutive years and is now 'very close' to meeting demand per VP Jun He. VP confirms 5.5x reticle CoWoS in mass production with 98%+ yields. ABF substrate shortage flagged as next bottleneck after memory. Sony-TSMC JV in Kumamoto announced for $4.7B.

bullets.title: SNDK Investor Day: 80% Gross Margin Target Through FY2030; $93.9B Contracted
bullets.body: SanDisk 2026 Investor Day targets mid-to-high teens revenue growth and 80% non-GAAP gross margin by FY2028–2030. CFO disclosed $93.9B in total contracted value from 8 customers over life of contracts with 100% shareholder cash return. Flash market projected $300B+ in 2026 and ~$500B in 2027. NAND market analyst adds 332-layer BiCS 10 QLC platform as next key product cycle.

bullets.title: MU Keybanc Chat: Contracts Extend Beyond 2030; Memory Structurally Different
bullets.body: Micron EVP at Keybanc conference confirms deep customer engineering engagements with roadmap visibility beyond 2030. Analyst 14546264 notes LTAs show 'waterfall dynamics' suggesting structural (not cyclical) memory demand. MU and SNDK highlighted as store-of-value hard assets by institutional accounts; server DDR5 prices rose 15–23% in August.

bullets.title: NVDA Vera Rubin Ramp Squeezes TLC NAND; 512Gb Spot Rises to $21
bullets.body: NVIDIA's Vera Rubin GPU production ramp is squeezing TLC NAND supply and lifting 512Gb spot prices to $21 after a June decline. TLC spot prices have started recovering ahead of the ramp per multiple supply-chain observers. HBM memory to constitute 62% of Vera Rubin BoM; Rubin Ultra downspec from HBM4 to HBM4E (8-high and 12-high) reportedly boosts unit supply.

bullets.title: AAPL: US Pressures on Chinese Memory; Apple Manufacturing Expands
bullets.body: Lutnick and US government pressing Apple not to use Chinese memory chips (CXMT/YMTC) for national security reasons, though Apple says it must consider 'all options.' Apple reported CXMT chip testing for iPhone models. Meanwhile, Apple opened an Advanced Manufacturing Center in Houston for Mac mini/AI server production and launched $600B US manufacturing commitment. Jefferies cuts AAPL to Underperform on all-glass iPhone cancellation and challenging premium pricing roadmap.

bullets.title: Meta Releases Muse Glimmer Open-Weight Model; META Compute Lens
bullets.body: Meta released Muse Glimmer (30B parameter) as open weights, running on a single consumer GPU, and Spark 1.2 as open weights—seen as strategic move to compete with Chinese open-source labs. Secretary Bessent welcomed the release as an American innovation win. Analyst note: META's internal LLM lab compute spending ($1.4T capex commitment) should not be used to estimate core business margins. META stock hit multi-week highs on the launch day.

bullets.title: SPX/VIX: Call Skew at 2-Year Highs; Market Breadth at 73% Above 200-DMA
bullets.body: SPX call skew near 2-year highs with put skew at 2-year lows—analyst flags crowded bullish setup but warns Trump/Bessent policy backdrop makes fading dangerous. 73% of Nasdaq 100 stocks now trade above their 200-day MA (best breadth in 13 months). VIX touched 7-month lows (~14.3) as structured Asian products dampen single-stock vol. SPY has ~$10B positive gamma at 780 strike.

bullets.title: GOOGL Capital Returns and AI Strategy: Sergey Brin Pushes Gemini
bullets.body: Google CEO confirms Gemini reached 1B+ monthly users (fastest-growing Google product ever, 14th to hit 1B milestone). Sergey Brin urged staff to advance Gemini to the frontier. GOOGL completed $200B capex guidance for 2026, turning FCF negative in Q2 (-$5B). Analyst Chip Stock Investor model projects GOOGL should allocate capex toward TPU/AI datacenter over model R&D for superior ROIC.

bullets.title: CSCO Q4 FY26 Blowout: $17.3B Revenue +18% YoY; Q1 Guidance 2x Consensus
bullets.body: Cisco Q4 FY26 revenue $17.3B (vs. $16.83B est), +18% YoY. Non-GAAP EPS $1.22 (+23% YoY). Q1 guidance: revenue $18.0–18.2B (vs. $16.84B est) and EPS $1.32–1.34 (vs. $1.17 est). Product revenue grew 24%. Melius raises PT to $160. Analyst note confirms AI infrastructure spending reaching networking/enterprise hardware layer.

bullets.title: Macro: US July CPI In-Line; SPR at 40-Year Low; 30Y Yield at 25-Year High
bullets.body: July CPI met expectations: headline +3.4% YoY, core +2.5% YoY, exactly as forecast—easing September rate-hike pressure to 36-44% odds. UMich consumer sentiment crashed to 51.0 (vs. 55.0 est) in August, weakest since 2008; 1-year inflation expectations rose to 4.3%. US SPR fell below 300M barrels (lowest since 1983). 30-year Treasury auction hit 5.216% yield (25-year high). Atlanta Fed GDPNow Q3 cut to 4.3% from 5.8%.

bullets.title: AMD Raises $5B Debt; Venice CPU Outperforms in Agent Sandboxes
bullets.body: AMD raised $4.75B in its largest-ever bond offering to fund AI expansion. AMD Venice CPU (256 cores, 400W) described as vastly outperforming Vera (Nvidia) for agentic sandbox workloads and 2x more power-efficient. UBS expects AMD to pursue Intel foundry partnership. AMD ranked #23 on IBD Top 50; chart forming bullish 50-day consolidation.
